cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Book ≠ screen – a written work printed on paper or shown online.

p.em: Example: I read a book every night before sleep.

cosy-blockquote.p: Love ≠ hate – to like something very much.

p.em: Example: Children love stories about magic and animals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Read ≠ write – to look at words and understand their meaning.

p.em: Example: She likes to read in the quiet garden.

cosy-blockquote.p: Story ≠ fact – a description of imaginary or real people and events.

p.em: Example: My grandfather told us a funny story.

cosy-blockquote.p: Library ≠ store – a room or building containing books to borrow.

p.em: Example: We get five books from the library each week.

cosy-blockquote.p: Page ≠ cover – one side of a piece of paper in a book.

p.em: Example: Turn to page ten to see the picture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Quiet ≠ loud – making very little noise.

p.em: Example: Please be quiet in the reading room.

cosy-blockquote.p: Author ≠ reader – a person who writes books.

p.em: Example: Who is your favorite author?

cosy-blockquote.p: Cover ≠ inside – the outside part of a book.

p.em: Example: The book has a bright blue cover.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bookmark – a piece of paper used to mark your place in a book.

p.em: Example: I use a colorful paper bookmark.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What kind of book do you like to read in your free time?
★ What was your favorite childhood story?

Do you love buying paper books or reading digital ebooks?
★ How many books do you read in a month?

Where is your favorite quiet place to read at home?
★ Do you read before going to sleep?

Who is a famous author from your country?
★ Have you ever met a published writer?

How often do you visit a public library or local bookstore?
★ Did you borrow books from libraries as a student?

Do you use a pretty bookmark or fold the corner of a page?
★ Do you collect handmade bookmarks?

Does an attractive book cover make you want to read it?
★ Have you ever judged a book by its cover?

What interesting story did a friend recommend to you recently?
★ Do you share book recommendations with friends?

How many pages can you read in one sitting?
★ Do you read fast or slow?

Why do people enjoy time to read during summer holidays?
★ What book are you reading right now?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Paper books are much better than digital e-readers. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you own an e-reader device?

Listening to an audiobook is the same as reading a physical book. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you listen to audiobooks while commuting?

Public library buildings will always remain important community centers. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ When did you last visit your neighborhood library?

Every child should learn to love reading at an early age. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Who taught you how to read?

A compelling story in a book is always better than its movie adaptation. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What movie adaptation disappointed you?

A famous author has a duty to teach moral lessons in their books. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Which author inspired you the most?

Reading in a quiet environment is essential for deep focus. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Can you read with background music or noise?

Using a proper bookmark shows respect for physical books. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What do you use to mark your page?

Designing a striking book cover is as important as writing good text. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Have you bought a book just for its design?

Reading 10 pages every single day can change a person's habits. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you set daily reading goals?

ul.li: Incorrect: I like to reading books. → Correct: I like reading books. ((Use 'like + verb-ing' or 'like + to + infinitive', not both together.))
Incorrect: She read every day. → Correct: She reads every day. ((Present simple 3rd person singular needs '-s': 'she reads'.))
